attribution.title: The Hornbill
attribution.author: Bukheye Mulongo Christopher

pages.text:
As I was moving in
Buŋaanga village I
found a fat hornbill.

When I struck it with a
catapult, it shouted
"ŋaa, ŋaa, ŋa!"

The hornbill flew into
the air.
But I ran after it
through the grass...

...until it perched on a
dead tree.
Then I shot it again.
This time it fell to the
ground.

And I gave it to
Hiryagaana: one who
eats whatever he finds.
(One time, I gave him
Namupongera.)
He happily received the
hornbill.

The head of the hornbill
was very big and as
hard as a panga or
machete.

The bird had fat like
that of a sheep.
It was so appetising!

It's not easy to find a
hornbill without
planning.
At night, hornbills roost
on dry branches.
A person eats what he
likes.
That is why Hiryagaana
eats hornbills.
